en: Since the knowledge of Brahman arises from merely hearing it once, this *Brahmajñānāvalīmālā* is for the attainment of liberation for all. (1)
I am unattached, I am unattached, I am unattached again and again;
I am the form of existence, consciousness, and bliss; I alone am the imperishable Self. ||2||
I am eternally pure and liberated; I am formless and immutable.
I am the very nature of the bliss of the Infinite; I alone am the imperishable Self. ||3||
I am eternal, I am faultless, I am said to be formless;
I am the nature of supreme bliss, I alone am the imperishable Self. ||4||
I am the nature of pure consciousness, and I alone am one who delights in the Self;
I am the form of indivisible bliss, and I alone am the imperishable I. ||5||
I am the nature of immediate consciousness; I am peaceful, beyond primordial nature (prakṛti);
I am the form of eternal bliss; I alone am the imperishable Self.
I am the Supreme Self, transcending reality; I am the supreme Śiva, beyond the intermediate state;
I alone am the imperishable, the supreme light, transcending Māyā. ||7||
I am beyond all diverse forms; I am the form of consciousness, the infallible one.
I am the very nature of the form of bliss; I alone am the imperishable Self.
Illusion, its effects such as the body and so forth, never exist for me at all;
I am of the singular nature of self-luminosity, I alone am the imperishable Self. (9)
I am beyond the three qualities (guṇas), and I am the witness of Brahmā and the other gods;
I possess infinite and endless forms, and I alone am the imperishable Self.
I am the nature of the Inner Controller, the immutable, and all-pervading;
I am the nature of the Supreme Self, I alone am the imperishable.
I am partless, I am actionless, the primordial Self of all, eternal;
I am the directly perceived essential nature, I alone am I, the imperishable.
I am the witness of dualities and the like; I am immovable and eternal.
I am the very nature of the witness of all; I alone am the immutable Self.
I am indeed a mass of pure consciousness and a mass of discernment;
I am neither an agent nor an enjoyer; I alone am the immutable Self. 14.
I am of a nature that is without support, and I alone am the support of all;
I am of a nature whose desires are fulfilled, and I alone am the imperishable Self. ||15||
Freed from the threefold suffering, distinct from the three bodies, and the witness of the three states—I am indeed that immutable Self alone. 16.
There are two categories of objects, the Seer and the Seen, which are mutually distinct.
"The Seer is Brahman and the Seen is Māyā"—this is the drumbeat of all the Vedāntas. (17)
"He who knows, 'I am the witness,' having thus discriminated again and again—he alone is liberated, he is the wise one; such is the drumbeat of Vedānta. (18)
Just as everything such as a pot or a wall is nothing but clay, so too is the entire universe Brahman; such is the proclamation of the Vedānta. 19.
"Brahman is reality, the world is illusory; the individual soul is none other than Brahman itself.
By this, the drum of Vedānta proclaims that true scripture is that which reveals this. (20)
The inner light, the outer light, the inward-facing light, higher than the highest;
the light of lights, the self-luminous light, the light of the Self—I am Śiva. 21.

Thus ends the *Brahmajñānāvalīmālā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (*paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya*).
